title: He confessed sins he didn’t personally commit.
paragraphs: He confessed sins he didn’t personally commit.
Let that disturb you for a second.

Because most of us?
We’re experts at distancing ourselves from sin.

“But that’s not me.”
“I’m not like them.”
“At least I didn’t go that far.”

Not because he was guilty of everything—
but because he understood something we’ve forgotten.

And if you miss this…
you’ll keep praying shallow prayers your whole life.

Daniel was living right…
while his nation was living wrong.

He had integrity in a culture of compromise.
Conviction in a generation of rebellion.
“We have sinned and done wrong. We have been wicked and have rebelled…” — Daniel 9:5
Because we like separating ourselves from brokenness.
We like standing on the moral high ground.
He said, “God, start with us… start with me.”
Let me get real with you.
Some of you are carrying secret sin.

Hidden pride.
Quiet lust.
Spiritual arrogance.
Unforgiveness dressed as “boundaries.”
Comparison masked as “discernment.”
And you’ve learned how to function with it.

Smile in public.
Serve in ministry.
Post the verse.
Say the prayer.

In your worship.
In your quiet time.
In the silence when you try to pray.
Because God doesn’t move through performance.
“The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit; a broken and contrite heart, O God, you will not despise.”
And then he says something that flips the entire script:
“We do not make requests of You because we are righteous, but because of Your great mercy.” — Daniel 9:18
Prayer is no longer about how good you are.
It’s about how good God is.
And this is where many people miss the Gospel.

You can’t fix yourself.
You can’t cleanse your own sin.
You can’t stand before a holy God on your own goodness.
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.”

That includes the obvious sinner…
and the quiet churchgoer.

The rebellious prodigal…
and the disciplined Daniel-type.
We are all in need of mercy.
On the cross, something shocking happened.
He stepped in and said, in effect:
“God made Him who had no sin to be sin for us, so that in Him we might become the righteousness of God.”

Jesus took your sin…
your hidden sin…
your repeated sin…
your shame…
And carried it to the cross.
“He was pierced for our transgressions, He was crushed for our iniquities… and by His wounds we are healed.”
That means your story isn’t stuck.
But here’s the part most people avoid:

“God, I stop defending this.
I stop hiding this.
I bring it into Your light.”
“If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just and will forgive us our sins and purify us from all unrighteousness.”
So why are you still holding on?
Why are you still negotiating with the very thing Jesus died to free you from?
And that means your sin is not something to manage.
Close your eyes for a moment.

Where have you been saying “they”…
when God is calling you to say “we”?

Where have you been justifying…
what God is gently exposing?

Where have you been performing…
instead of surrendering?
He is not waiting to condemn you.
He is ready to restore you.
“There is therefore now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.”

“Lord… I stop hiding.
I stop pretending.
I bring You all of me.
Have mercy on me.
Change me.
I trust in Jesus alone.”
And if this stirred something deep in your spirit…
